results.title: Coroutines and tasks — Python 3.14.7 documentation
results.snippet: To prevent aw from being cancelled, wrap it in shield(). The function will wait until the future is actually cancelled, so the total wait time may exceed the timeout. If an exception happens during cancellation, it is propagated.

results.title: Asyncio Shield From Cancellation – SuperFastPython
results.snippet: A coroutine passed to shield() will be wrapped in an asyncio.Task and scheduled immediately. The Future returned from shield() does not need to be awaited in order for the provided coroutine to be executed. We can wait for a shielded task to complete by keeping a reference to the asyncio.Task ...

results.title: python asyncio - how to wait for a cancelled shielded task? - Stack Overflow
results.snippet: If the cancelled coroutine is finishes before the shielded task finishes (in run_until_complete) then the shielded task is not actually waited for. Why doesnt the implementation of shield just do await real_task? 2018-09-26T14:36:26.517Z+00:00 ... @shane If shield alyways awaited the task it protects, then its cancellation would be a no-op. (The new docs explain how to get such effect if needed.) This would mean that e.g. asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(foo()), 1) would always wait for foo() to finish, which is undesirable.
